## 📅 **Timeline of Key Events at the Design Museum of Chicago (DMoC)**

| **Year** | **Event** | **Details** |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **2012** | **Founded as a pop-up museum** | Tanner Woodford founded the Design Museum of Chicago (formerly Chicago Design Museum) as a temporary, pop-up exhibition space. Exhibitions were held in various venues across Chicago. |
| **2013** | **Continued pop-up exhibitions** | The museum expanded its presence through rotating pop-up exhibitions in different Chicago locations. |
| **2014** | **Successful Kickstarter campaign** | The museum launched a crowdfunding campaign on Kickstarter, which was highly successful and provided the funds needed to establish a permanent home. |
| **2014** | **Opened permanent location** | The museum moved into the **Block 37 building** in Chicago, marking its first permanent space. |
| **2018** | **Relocated to Expo 72** | The museum moved to its current location at **72 E. Randolph Street (Expo 72)**, a more central and accessible venue. |
| **2021** | **Health Art Campaign** | Partnered with the **Chicago Department of Public Health** and **Chicago Department of Cultural Affairs** to commission over **80 local artists** to create art on themes of **health, vitality, community, and vaccine distribution**. Art was displayed on billboards and social media to encourage vaccination. |
| **2021–Present** | **Great Ideas of Humanity series** | Contemporary artists and designers respond to quotes from scientists, philosophers, and academics (e.g., Goethe, Rumi, Mary Wollstonecraft). Artwork is displayed on **downtown bus transit stanchions** and shown internationally at events like **Hong Kong’s InnoTech Design Expo**. |
| **2021–Present** | **Chicago Design Market** | A rotating pop-up series on the 3rd floor of Block 37. Small emerging artists and established brands (e.g., Cards Against Humanity, Aviate Press, Fourneau Bread Oven) share retail space. No fixed rent—museum takes a **sales commission** to support the program. |
| **2021–Present** | **Design Pack (Cards Against Humanity expansion)** | A non-profit expansion pack featuring 30 illustrated cards based on George Carlin’s “Seven Words You Can Never Say on Television.” All proceeds go to DMoC. Sales exceeded **$130,000** in early days. Similar packs have raised millions for other nonprofits. |
| **2023–2026** | **Logo Design** | The museum’s current logo was designed by the **Substance Collective**, a Chicago-based group. The design reflects the city’s **urban grid** and the **interconnectivity of neighborhoods, streets, and communities**. |
| **January 31, 2026** | **Leadership Transition** | **Tanner Woodford stepped down as Executive Director** after nearly 14 years. He remains involved as **Founder and Board Member**, continuing to support the museum’s mission. |
